openings.claim: Stronger corner compression need not be necessary for lateral registration: reversible edge stops could carry the sideways load while the hatch rests on its existing seal.
openings.delta: Remove deliberate left-corner tightening. Replace dependence on seal friction with lateral bearing against strip stops, attached through padded, reversible rim clamps. Cut supplied strips into paired jaws if feasible; drill only strips. Stops and recoverable cord-tethered parts must stay outside the marked opening or be removed within the reopening limit. Use no straps or powered mechanism.
openings.prediction: If positive lateral bearing suffices, ten closures without corner tightening retain the hatch within 1 mm under 20 N, including the final right-card disturbance, without seal tears and with reopening within 30 seconds. The nearest rival is ordinary compression-dependent friction: it predicts resistance should disappear without preload. Successful registration with no deliberate preload and unchanged seal condition would counter the necessity claim; it would not establish that compression never works or that stops are necessary.
openings.probe: First check whether supplied strip pairs, bolt lengths and rim geometry permit removable, nondeforming clamps and lateral stops without obstructing the opening; otherwise park this probe. Allocate two ordinary centered-hatch trials, one with left-corner pressing and one disturbed, releasing the hand before pulling. Then perform ten stop-configuration opening/closure/pull trials, the tenth disturbed. Record marked displacement, opposite-corner lift, visible seal condition and reopening time with the supplied instruments. Stop on damage; interrupted testing cannot establish the outcome. This uses twelve trials and two configurations, each disturbed once.
assumptions: An accessible rim feature, sufficient bolt length and workable strip shaping permit four stable clamp/stop stations using only supplied tools, strips, bolts and pads; these are unprovided geometric and fabrication facts.
The cord can keep removed parts recoverable without obstructing inspection or slowing reopening beyond 30 seconds.

Defeat conditions include clamp migration, hatch riding over stops, disturbance-induced rocking exceeding registration tolerance, damage, infeasible fabrication within ninety minutes, or observation exceeding twenty minutes.
Residual seal friction remains a rival explanation; successful stopping alone does not isolate its contribution or demonstrate deployment reliability.

assessment: A conditional counterexample candidate, with uncertain attachment feasibility; no supplied observation establishes success. Ordinary corner pressing remains a comparison, not a proven satisfactory joint.
